# Listbox

> A list of Options to pick one or more from, right on the page instead of in a popup.

`<slab-listbox>` · Selection · built on `[role=listbox]`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/listbox/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/listbox.js';
import 'slab-elements/option.js';
import 'slab-elements/option-group.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-listbox label="Size" name="size">
  <slab-option value="s">Small</slab-option>
  <slab-option value="m" selected>Medium</slab-option>
  <slab-option value="l">Large</slab-option>
</slab-listbox>
```

Option, documented here, is also what [Select](select.md) and
[Combobox](combobox.md) use.

To group Options under a heading, put them in a `slab-option-group` with a `label`. It's a `[role=group]` named by its label, and its Options are still the Listbox's, so the keys and selection work across groups as across the rest. Select and Combobox take Option Groups too, and Combobox hides one while its filter hides every Option in it.

```html
<slab-listbox label="Produce">
  <slab-option-group label="Fruit">
    <slab-option>Apple</slab-option>
    <slab-option>Banana</slab-option>
  </slab-option-group>

  <slab-option-group label="Vegetables">
    <slab-option>Carrot</slab-option>
  </slab-option-group>
</slab-listbox>
```

## Long lists

For thousands of Options, set `virtual`. Only the Options in or near view are laid out, and spacers take the room of the rest, so the scrollbar is the size it would be with all of them. The Options are still all there, so the keys, typeahead, selection and the form value reach every one, and the list scrolls to whichever becomes active. Each Option that's rendered gets `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize`, so a screenreader still says "4 of 5,000".

Give `::part(listbox)` a block size so it scrolls. Options are taken to be the same height as each other, which is measured from the ones on screen.

```html
<style>
  slab-listbox::part(listbox) {
    block-size: 20rem;
  }
</style>

<slab-listbox label="City" virtual>
  <slab-option>Aachen</slab-option>
  <slab-option>Aalborg</slab-option>
  <!-- And thousands more -->
</slab-listbox>
```

## Keyboard

| Key          | What it does                                                              |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Up, Down     | Moves the active Option, stopping at each end and skipping disabled ones. |
| Home, End    | Moves to the first or last Option.                                        |
| A character  | Moves to the next Option whose label starts with what's typed.            |
| Enter, Space | Selects the active Option, or toggles it when `multiple` is set.          |

With `multiple`, Shift with Up or Down moves and toggles, Shift with Space
selects from the last selected Option to the active one, Control or Command
with Shift and Home or End selects from the active one to the first or last,
and Control or Command with A selects every Option, or none.

## Elements

### `<slab-listbox>`

Import `slab-elements/listbox.js` to register it.

A list of Options to select one or more from, with no visual styles.

There's no native listbox: `<select>` draws its own options, and they can't be anything but text. So this is a `<div role="listbox">` and ARIA does the rest. Not a `<ul>`: a list may only hold list items, which neither a slot nor an Option is, and the role would replace its semantics anyway.

Options are found by class rather than by tag name, so your subclass of Option can be named anything.

Focus stays on the listbox, and the active Option is pointed at with `aria-activedescendant` rather than focused, the way the APG's own listbox does it. It's what lets a Combobox keep focus in its input while the user moves through the Options, and a Select keep it on its button. Read or set the active Option with `activeOption`.

The arrow keys, Home and End move the active Option, stopping at each end and skipping disabled Options. Typing moves it to the next Option whose label starts with what was typed. Space, Enter, and a click select it, or toggle it when `multiple` is set. Then, as in the APG's multi-select listbox, Shift with an arrow key moves and toggles, Shift with Space selects every Option from the one last selected to the active one, Control or Command with Shift and Home or End selects every Option from the active one to the first or last and moves there, and Control or Command with A selects every Option, or none when all of them already are.

Style it through its parts and through `:state(disabled)`, `:state(error)`, and `:state(required)`, and each Option through `:state(active)`, `:state(disabled)`, and `:state(selected)`.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type      | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------ | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` (required) | `string`  |         | Names it. It's the accessible name, and the visible label where there is one.                                                                                                      |
| `disabled`         | `boolean` | `false` | Disables it, as `disabled` does a native control: the user can't focus or use it, and a form control's value isn't submitted.                                                      |
| `hide-label`       | `boolean` | `false` | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way.                                                                   |
| `multiple`         | `boolean` | `false` | Lets more than one be selected at a time.                                                                                                                                          |
| `name`             | `string`  | `''`    | The name its value is submitted under, as a native control's `name`.                                                                                                               |
| `required`         | `boolean` | `false` | Makes it invalid while it has no value, as `required` does a native control.                                                                                                       |
| `virtual`          | `boolean` | `false` | Lays out only the Options in or near view, for a Listbox with thousands. Give `::part(listbox)` a block size so it scrolls. Options are taken to be the same height as each other. |
| `value`            | `string`  | `''`    | The value of the first selected and enabled Option. Setting it selects the Option with that value, and only that one. Not reflected, to match a native control.                    |

#### Properties

| Name                            | Type                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `defaultValue`                  | `string`                  | The value it selects when none of its Options has `selected`, and goes back to when its form resets. It's the `value` attribute, so setting it sets the attribute, and `value` with it. |
| `activeOption`                  | `Option \| null`          | The Option the user is on, which Space, Enter and typeahead act from. It's pointed at rather than focused, so focus stays where it is.                                                  |
| `form` (read-only)              | `HTMLFormElement \| null` | The form it belongs to, or `null`.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `options` (read-only)           | `Option[]`                | Its Options, in order.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `selectedOptions` (read-only)   | `Option[]`                | Selected and enabled Options, in the order they appear.                                                                                                                                 |
| `validationMessage` (read-only) | `string`                  | What's wrong, as the validity message says it: the message given to `setCustomValidity()` or `setValidity()`, or else the browser's own. Empty while it's valid.                        |
| `validity` (read-only)          | `ValidityState`           | Its `ValidityState`, as a native control's.                                                                                                                                             |
| `willValidate` (read-only)      | `boolean`                 | Whether its validity is checked when its form submits. It isn't while it's disabled or read-only.                                                                                       |
| `values`                        | `string[]`                | The value of every selected and enabled Option, in the order they appear. Setting it selects the Options with those values, and only those.                                             |

#### Methods

| Signature                                                         | Description                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checkValidity(): boolean`                                        | Whether its value is valid. Dispatches "invalid" when it isn't, as a native control's does.                                   |
| `focus(options?: FocusOptions): void`                             | Focuses it, or the part of it that takes focus.                                                                               |
| `reportValidity(): boolean`                                       | Whether its value is valid. When it isn't, dispatches "invalid" and shows the validity message, as a native control's does.   |
| `resetValidityFeedback(): void`                                   | Clears the validity feedback without changing `validity`.                                                                     |
| `setCustomValidity(message: string): void`                        | Makes it invalid with a message of your own, or valid again with an empty one, as a native control's does.                    |
| `setValidity(flags?: ValidityStateFlags, message?: string): void` | Sets its validity and message, as `ElementInternals.setValidity()` does, for checks of your own beyond `setCustomValidity()`. |

#### Events

| Name      | Type    | Description                                                                                                        |
| --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `input`   | `Event` | As the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.               |
| `change`  | `Event` | When the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.             |
| `invalid` | `Event` | When a check finds its value invalid, as a native control's does. Cancel it to leave the validity message unshown. |

#### Slots

| Name          | Type                    | Description                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| (default)     | `Option \| OptionGroup` |                                                                                                             |
| `description` | `Element \| string`     | Text that describes it, such as a hint or what the validity message means. It's its accessible description. |

#### CSS parts

| Name               | Description                                                      |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description`      | Text about the Listbox, and its validity message when it has one |
| `label`            | The label                                                        |
| `listbox`          | The Options                                                      |
| `validity-message` | The validity message, which says why the value is invalid        |

#### CSS states

| Name               | Description                                                                                                               |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(disabled)` | While it's disabled.                                                                                                      |
| `:state(error)`    | While it's invalid and its validity message shows, which is once its validity is reported, as when its form is submitted. |
| `:state(required)` | While it's required, for styles such as an asterisk.                                                                      |

### `<slab-option>`

Import `slab-elements/option.js` to register it.

An Option with no visual styles. The host is the option, so style it directly.

It's never focused. Focus stays on its Listbox, which points at the active Option with `aria-activedescendant`, so a Select or a Combobox can keep focus where it is while the user moves through the Options.

Its Listbox sets `:state(active)`. It sets `:state(disabled)`, which is also set while its Listbox is disabled, and `:state(selected)` itself.

#### Attributes

| Name       | Type      | Default | Description                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------- | --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `label`    | `string`  |         | Names the Option in place of its text, and is what typeahead matches against.                                                                    |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables it, as `disabled` does a native control: the user can't focus or use it, and a form control's value isn't submitted.                    |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Like a native option, the attribute is the default state and the property is the current one. Style `:state(selected)` rather than `[selected]`. |
| `value`    | `string`  | `''`    | Its label, or its text when it has no label, when not set. The same as a native option.                                                          |

#### Properties

| Name               | Type      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------ | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `defaultSelected`  | `boolean` | Whether it starts selected, and is selected again when its form resets. It's the `selected` attribute, as a native option's `defaultSelected` is, so setting it sets the attribute, and `selected` with it. |
| `text` (read-only) | `string`  | What the user reads as the Option's name: its label, or its text when it has no label.                                                                                                                      |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type                | Description                                              |
| --------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| (default) | `Element \| string` | The label, plus anything else a design puts in an Option |

#### CSS states

| Name               | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(active)`   | While it's the active one, which the keyboard moves through while focus stays on its container. |
| `:state(disabled)` | While it's disabled.                                                                            |
| `:state(selected)` | While it's selected.                                                                            |

### `<slab-option-group>`

Import `slab-elements/option-group.js` to register it.

An Option Group with no visual styles: a named `[role=group]` of Options, such as "Fruit" and "Vegetables", inside a Listbox, Select or Combobox.

The host is the group, so style it directly. Its Options are still its Listbox's, Select's or Combobox's, so the arrow keys, typeahead and selection work across them as across the rest. A Combobox hides an Option Group while its filter hides every Option in it.

Its label is rendered, for sighted users, and hidden from screenreaders, which hear it as the group's name from `aria-label` instead. `hide-label` hides it visually too.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type      | Default | Description                                                                                                      |
| ------------------ | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` (required) | `string`  |         | Names it. It's the accessible name, and the visible label where there is one.                                    |
| `hide-label`       | `boolean` | `false` | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way. |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type     | Description |
| --------- | -------- | ----------- |
| (default) | `Option` |             |

#### CSS parts

| Name    | Description |
| ------- | ----------- |
| `label` | The label   |
